pr_title: lang/funcs: Redact sensitive values from function errors
pr_body:
Some function errors include values derived from arguments. This commit is the result of a manual audit of these errors, which resulted in:

- Adding a helper function to redact sensitive values;
- Applying that helper function where errors include values derived from possibly-sensitive arguments;
- Cleaning up other errors which need not include those values, or were otherwise incorrect.

Fixes #30033

## Example

```shellsession
$ echo 'base64decode("wheee")' | terraform console
╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│
│   on <console-input> line 1:
│   (source code not available)
│
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: failed to decode base64 data "wheee".
╵

$ echo 'base64decode(sensitive("wheee"))' | terraform console
╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│
│   on <console-input> line 1:
│   (source code not available)
│
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: failed to decode base64 data (sensitive value).
╵
```

Hi @tobias-ds24, thanks for reporting this. I'm not able to reproduce the issue, as the error message does not seem to include the sensitive value:

```shellsession
$ echo 'base64decode(sensitive("test"))' | terraform-1.0.11 console
╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│
│   on <console-input> line 1:
│   (source code not available)
│
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: the result of decoding the provided string is not
│ valid UTF-8.
╵
```

Can you explain what you're seeing that caused you to file this issue?

Hi @alisdair, you're right, I oversimplified my minimal example, sorry about that:

```
variable "secret" {
  type = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "null_resource" "test" {
  triggers = {
    value = base64decode(var.secret)
  }
}
```
interestingly enough, when I call this with: `terraform apply -var=secret=supersecretvalue` ,  the output is
```
╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│ 
│   on main.tf line 7, in resource "null_resource" "test":
│    7:     value = base64decode(var.secret)
│     ├────────────────
│     │ var.secret has a sensitive value
│ 
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: the result of decoding the provided string is not valid UTF-8.
```
but when I enter the value interactively, it is logged (while still being claimed as sensitive):
```
terraform apply
var.secret
  Enter a value: dfg

╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│ 
│   on main.tf line 7, in resource "null_resource" "test":
│    7:     value = base64decode(var.secret)
│     ├────────────────
│     │ var.secret has a sensitive value
│ 
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: failed to decode base64 data 'dfg'.
```

I can't easily share my original code, it was reading a secret from an `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` `secret_string`, which is also marked "sensitive"

Ah, I see, thanks! The error message returned from the function is dependent on the value passed. I think any input with an odd number of characters will result in revealing the sensitive value. Example:

```shellsession
$ echo 'base64decode(sensitive("wheee"))' | terraform-1.0.11 console
╷
│ Error: Error in function call
│
│   on <console-input> line 1:
│   (source code not available)
│
│ Call to function "base64decode" failed: failed to decode base64 data 'wheee'.
╵
```

I'm able to reproduce this and will take a look at what's involved with fixing it.

review_comments: To me the marks on the input path seem logically distinct from the boolean existence of a file. While the input may clearly be _sensitive_, should using that cause the result to be sensitive? I guess it follows pretty closely to the fact that using the input in a conditional would cause the conditional result to retain the same marks, but just wanted to pose the question in case we don't really need cause the marks to propagate through here too.

The existing implementation (using the automatic re-marking from cty) does mark the result as sensitive:

```shellsession
$ tf console
> fileexists("main.tf")
false
> fileexists(sensitive("main.tf"))
(sensitive)
```

I don't think that's particularly useful, assuming that we don't intend the sensitive value implementation to protect against side-channel attacks. I'll plan to remove the marks from this function, but if anyone disagrees with that change I'm happy to leave them in.

There is a small hazard here that someone was using `nonsensitive(fileexists(...))` to achieve this effect before and would now need to remove the `nonsensitive`. I don't know how likely it is, but I mention it in case you think it might affect the risk/reward tradeoff.

That does make me more nervous about removing the marks. I hadn't thought of this situation where it breaks compatibility, no matter how unlikely it is. Given that we don't have any users requesting this change or considering it a bug, I'll leave it as-is for now.
